expected_output.reasoning:
The investigation correctly identifies the single attacking client 198.51.100.40 running a multi-vector injection probe (SQLi, XSS, path traversal, SSRF — matching the expected list minus explicit Log4J mention) against the CloudFront distribution. It identifies that the WAF managed rule groups (CommonRuleSet, SQLi Rule Set) blocked the bulk of the probes (~180, close to the expected ~210) returning 403s, which is a correct mitigation. Critically, it also identifies the exact same gap as the expected root cause: 15 requests with the LFI probe `file=/proc/self/environ` were ALLOWED through because no managed rule matched this specific pattern — a WAF coverage gap, not a misconfiguration. This matches the expected root cause's core finding: ~210 blocked (correct mitigation), ~15 allowed due to missed-by-rule (GenericLFI_QUERYARGUMENTS pattern not matching this specific LFI variant). The numbers are slightly different (180 vs 210 blocked, total ~195 vs ~225) and the investigation doesn't mention Log4J specifically or the exact rule IDs, but the fundamental causal chain — single attacker running multi-vector probe, WAF blocked most, 15 LFI /proc/self/environ requests slipped through due to no matching rule — is correctly identified as both the cause and root cause.</reasoning>
<parameter name="evidence">"Of the attacker's traffic from 198.51.100.40, 15 requests were ALLOWed through to the EKS origin between 19:09:40 and 19:19:00 UTC — every one a local-file-inclusion probe: `GET /catalog?file=/proc/self/environ`... No managed rule (CommonRuleSet/SQLi/KnownBadInputs) matched this specific pattern, so WAF passed it with Default_Action=ALLOW... This is a confirmed WAF coverage gap with payloads that actually reached the application."
